Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 58, "heading": "CHAPTER 56. THE NEW WOUND, AND THE OLD", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 56, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u058-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 56. THE NEW WOUND, AND THE OLD", "sha256": "e09ee27c82f3e54a66a609a0510445d680a7a8324e420edbeabe32d44d16b543", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "No need, O Steerforth, to have said, when we last spoke together, in that hour which I so little deemed to be our parting-hour—no need to have said, ‘Think of me at my best!’ I had done that ever; and could I change now, looking on this sight!", "sha256": "e7c943135d678ac44ef98f1d491c0e563d6db7d8de3146ae0fa3ced8d7710581", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "They brought a hand-bier, and laid him on it, and covered him with a flag, and took him up and bore him on towards the houses. All the men who carried him had known him, and gone sailing with him, and seen him merry and bold. They carried him through the wild roar, a hush in the midst of all the tumult; and took him to the cottage where Death was already.", "sha256": "770e30c68c79b610166d250ef78fb9b034e0ef3b07158136eddfb8571c3829eb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But when they set the bier down on the threshold, they looked at one another, and at me, and whispered. I knew why. They felt as if it were not right to lay him down in the same quiet room.", "sha256": "9da209cb49fc6839ae979685e665e85fd1a01e0b7981caf85456ffb7961502c0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We went into the town, and took our burden to the inn. So soon as I could at all collect my thoughts, I sent for Joram, and begged him to provide me a conveyance in which it could be got to London in the night. I knew that the care of it, and the hard duty of preparing his mother to receive it, could only rest with me; and I was anxious to discharge that duty as faithfully as I could.", "sha256": "9a79ba60df4d3413be45621bf19bdea273329682685cf063cd27572b215cd5bb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I chose the night for the journey, that there might be less curiosity when I left the town. But, although it was nearly midnight when I came out of the yard in a chaise, followed by what I had in charge, there were many people waiting. At intervals, along the town, and even a little way out upon the road, I saw more: but at length only the bleak night and the open country were around me, and the ashes of my youthful friendship.", "sha256": "ab508e41fec8a8c8fc679ddd4990b15ce9d65fb670103d37499ef07d42fe82ae", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Upon a mellow autumn day, about noon, when the ground was perfumed by fallen leaves, and many more, in beautiful tints of yellow, red, and brown, yet hung upon the trees, through which the sun was shining, I arrived at Highgate. I walked the last mile, thinking as I went along of what I had to do; and left the carriage that had followed me all through the night, awaiting orders to advance.", "sha256": "42ded32d14a9e30b24a7431e8f38d980b1965a4d500a1a55c9d17d00558e1b93", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The house, when I came up to it, looked just the same. Not a blind was raised; no sign of life was in the dull paved court, with its covered way leading to the disused door. The wind had quite gone down, and nothing moved.", "sha256": "a83148406617fa7464ef34727823e5d141bb1241043314ce46c76664ca674a34", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had not, at first, the courage to ring at the gate; and when I did ring, my errand seemed to me to be expressed in the very sound of the bell. The little parlour-maid came out, with the key in her hand; and looking earnestly at me as she unlocked the gate, said:", "sha256": "ce41b7801d5ebdb94b3169961cea28b823f067aac565771d0b011792dd33a9c6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I beg your pardon, sir. Are you ill?’", "sha256": "eba0a7b2fec93f4169d1d4344ecc61578c9f3c5e1c9be4bcec789a3fcc560bed", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have been much agitated, and am fatigued.’", "sha256": "0b00479d4d05d391ee4d48623a78dd18fac817ffec7242218e995c29cc0ad3e1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is anything the matter, sir?—-Mr. James?—’ ‘Hush!’ said I. ‘Yes, something has happened, that I have to break to Mrs. Steerforth. She is at home?’", "sha256": "ee79fddca2d18a232f94be0c0eadbd8e9d242dd41d5386a36a9c31b92610415b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The girl anxiously replied that her mistress was very seldom out now, even in a carriage; that she kept her room; that she saw no company, but would see me. Her mistress was up, she said, and Miss Dartle was with her. What message should she take upstairs?", "sha256": "777fa21f7941df62f5a1a51e2efe71080631ee918933b2add22e10b97fabbd0b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Giving her a strict charge to be careful of her manner, and only to carry in my card and say I waited, I sat down in the drawing-room (which we had now reached) until she should come back. Its former pleasant air of occupation was gone, and the shutters were half closed. The harp had not been used for many and many a day. His picture, as a boy, was there. The cabinet in which his mother had kept his letters was there. I wondered if she ever read them now; if she would ever read them more!", "sha256": "612ea535ea7cf8bdd538cc3dcc7308eca1b0d39d380a3539db1a80f6dc08cc01", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The house was so still that I heard the girl’s light step upstairs. On her return, she brought a message, to the effect that Mrs. Steerforth was an invalid and could not come down; but that if I would excuse her being in her chamber, she would be glad to see me. In a few moments I stood before her.", "sha256": "f4ed1f30023dde41c833ada89c349bb9ce815dbe8ea745317a7fbfb1eae30c0c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She was in his room; not in her own. I felt, of course, that she had taken to occupy it, in remembrance of him; and that the many tokens of his old sports and accomplishments, by which she was surrounded, remained there, just as he had left them, for the same reason. She murmured, however, even in her reception of me, that she was out of her own chamber because its aspect was unsuited to her infirmity; and with her stately look repelled the least suspicion of the truth.", "sha256": "bdc4623e1e2aed4aa0fca1f60d9b2337618acb8478026ff2a72ffaaa98cb3e28", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At her chair, as usual, was Rosa Dartle. From the first moment of her dark eyes resting on me, I saw she knew I was the bearer of evil tidings. The scar sprung into view that instant. She withdrew herself a step behind the chair, to keep her own face out of Mrs. Steerforth’s observation; and scrutinized me with a piercing gaze that never faltered, never shrunk.", "sha256": "71b9ee220ad0634956f060517438a83e394d2d8f54444c27f3544b42283299b0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am sorry to observe you are in mourning, sir,’ said Mrs. Steerforth.", "sha256": "cd0c8d477cdc4e82a3c3810bd04a1c5d9dd14f9c2996e9870bafff9dcc5a85ba", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am unhappily a widower,’ said I.", "sha256": "39d9ad8ee5b283d6222c7da116cf3fe98df4a0d962bba17164c10224597796bb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You are very young to know so great a loss,’ she returned. ‘I am grieved to hear it. I am grieved to hear it. I hope Time will be good to you.’", "sha256": "03bbd80e2fecc9a794833b012f0abe0e63f550066e0c44c1518c97c496328ebf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I hope Time,’ said I, looking at her, ‘will be good to all of us. Dear Mrs. Steerforth, we must all trust to that, in our heaviest misfortunes.’", "sha256": "2eb0428ca6d44b8333eabc4547632ddec5ed3b008caa700fcca2269feb4d6e13", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The earnestness of my manner, and the tears in my eyes, alarmed her. The whole course of her thoughts appeared to stop, and change.", "sha256": "ac789835b8bf8e3f7c49f6db2d9fdae73e7958a9af27ffa9ee380b0b104fc662", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I tried to command my voice in gently saying his name, but it trembled. She repeated it to herself, two or three times, in a low tone. Then, addressing me, she said, with enforced calmness:", "sha256": "5bc8ca8915aaf8d55bdf16cbee9707e0fa915b9a2e46c4e2bf1f36402afe835a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My son is ill.’", "sha256": "270410da3a22976634a647a959f2aa168c3428c9f686fce3c22eba967483f3d6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Very ill.’", "sha256": "3ad909897157cf9c004d1fc8145935f53f62091323658b77d5a57ece45a46d17", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You have seen him?’", "sha256": "6c8b67aaba9c73aab9abc0ff7a26ef13f8726f0f0c9916ea7e7504f6d07f794e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have.’", "sha256": "4d6e835067270455b0190d360e4267bd3b56a026574c3ec0b5ca461ae4e55957", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Are you reconciled?’", "sha256": "01df8548b14fc91375ef4be936bb9af6d5606f16fcd1d28965e0f96ba0d6701b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I could not say Yes, I could not say No. She slightly turned her head towards the spot where Rosa Dartle had been standing at her elbow, and in that moment I said, by the motion of my lips, to Rosa, ‘Dead!’", "sha256": "a3b70a51e6d3533d29bdf3f1883061b0e05b43c2260f041e5be78a30dc55d9cc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "That Mrs. Steerforth might not be induced to look behind her, and read, plainly written, what she was not yet prepared to know, I met her look quickly; but I had seen Rosa Dartle throw her hands up in the air with vehemence of despair and horror, and then clasp them on her face.", "sha256": "8285546724c1eb26beed5a3d8ace31a90f1309bba6d77651f3be1bfe68f94fc8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "The handsome lady—so like, oh so like!—regarded me with a fixed look, and put her hand to her forehead. I besought her to be calm, and prepare herself to bear what I had to tell; but I should rather have entreated her to weep, for she sat like a stone figure.", "sha256": "e2f6cd9c318e8ceaefe7f510bc538f459383c61cae28c957fa46fd65a0930ac0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u058-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘When I was last here,’ I faltered, ‘Miss Dartle told me he was sailing here and there. The night before last was a dreadful one at sea. If he were at sea that night, and near a dangerous coast, as it is said he was; and if the vessel that was seen should really be the ship which—’", "sha256": "a3ad3cdcac97c6c85172630ebcbc4a27390da7945ff1a5289e6b7236a94d8e9a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[63]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
